title: RenderReportRequest
description: Request body for POST /api/reports/render. The service renders a .jrxml report from its configured reports directory and returns a PDF. Unknown top-level properties are ignored by the server, but are not part of the contract, so this schema rejects them.

reportFileName.description: Path of a .jrxml file relative to the service's reports directory. Use forward slashes for subdirectories (e.g. "purchasing/PurchaseOrder.jrxml"). Must end in .jrxml (the server's extension check ignores case). Backslashes and '..' segments are rejected: the resolved file must stay inside the reports directory.

parameters.description: Report parameters. Each array entry is an object holding one report parameter name and its value; the entries are merged into a single parameter map in order, so a name repeated in a later entry wins. Omit the property (or pass an empty array) when the report needs no parameters. Parameter names not declared by the report are ignored. A JSON value's type must match the class the report declares for that parameter exactly - the service performs no type conversion.

items.description: One {parameterName: parameterValue} pair. The server also accepts several pairs in one object, but the canonical form is one pair per entry.

propertyNames.description: A parameter name as declared by <parameter name="..."> in the .jrxml report.

additionalProperties.description: The parameter value. A JSON string maps to java.lang.String, an integer within int range to java.lang.Integer, a larger integer to java.lang.Long, a decimal to java.lang.Double, true/false to java.lang.Boolean, an array to java.util.ArrayList and an object to java.util.LinkedHashMap. Dates cannot be passed: no JSON type maps to java.util.Date. null is allowed and suppresses the report's own default value for that parameter.
